nodes.title: The gap measurement changed its own answer: writing exp-gap-002 into the graph dropped answeredAtBirth from 6 to 0
nodes.body:
e59 decides whether a gap is 'answered at birth' by finding a decimal percentage whose document frequency over all live nodes is <= 2. Then exp-gap-002 was written to record the result, and its body quotes all six percentages (42.8%, 49.3%, 26.6%, 42.46%, 24.5%, 40.4%). Each of those strings went from df=2 to df=3, so on the next run:

  gapsCarryingADistinctivePercentage: 7 -> 1
  answeredAtBirth: 6 -> 0
  rate: 0.273 -> 0

The measurement is not wrong at either time; the corpus changed. This is the third structural version of the same problem tonight: a quantity was reported without the population it was computed over (exp-stop-002's missing futility arm, exp-diff-002's 14 vs 7 disjoint sets, exp-dedup-001's gap list). Here the population was the graph at the moment of measurement, and the act of reporting moved it.

Fix applied: EXCLUDE = /^(exp-gap-|ana-023$)/ removes nodes that report on gaps from the frequency count, with the exclusions declared in code rather than inferred. Declaring them is honest about the shape of the problem: the alternative (snapshot the graph before every measurement) is not what a working graph is for, and any automatic 'exclude nodes that mention the threshold' rule would be circular.

Deeper point: a graph that holds both evidence and commentary on evidence will always have this tension. The convention that resolves it is one this graph already uses elsewhere -- measurements name their own source field, and nodes whose source is a research script are commentary, not evidence.

nodes.title: kg answer closes 6 of 320 questions, and a pack round trip carries them: 1437 nodes / 1477 edges / 174 decisions / 6 answers, byte-identical
nodes.body:
The gap list could not shrink: a question node has no transition out of status='live' and no edge to whatever answered it, so `kg gaps` was a monotone counter that printed 296 and then 320 regardless of what had been learned. Six of those 320 carried their own answer in the body (exp-gap-002).

Added two verbs and a table, deliberately parallel to `kg resolve`:
  gap_answer(gap_id PK, node_id, note, answered_at)
  kg answer <question> <node> --note "..."   (note required: an answer without a reason is indistinguishable from boredom)
  kg unanswer <question>                     (a wrong close must be reopenable)
  kg gaps                                    (default: unanswered only; --answered shows both with [answered by X])

Closed 6, each with the note naming which part of the question the node closes: gap-w7-030 -> n-post-promotion-spend, w2-human-gap-miss-rate-on-agent-diffs -> w2-human-automation-bias-ecg, gap-w4-030 -> w4-review-judge-skill-is-pair-property, gap-w5-022 -> w5-tokenbudget-half-spend-buys-nothing, cheapest-policy -> ledger-slots, gap-w7-007 -> n-loom-wasted-rounds. List goes 320 -> 314 of 320 asked.

Pack/unpack carries answers as `? <gap> <node> | note` blocks (an answer dropped in a round trip would silently reopen every question -- the exact defect pack had with resolutions). merge migrates gap_answer on both endpoints and drops rows where gap_id = node_id (a node cannot answer itself).

Full round trip verified: nodes +1437 · edges +1477 · decisions +174 · answers +6, cmp byte-identical both ways. tests/kg-answer.test.mjs 17/17 covers: note required, missing/invalid endpoints rejected, default list shrinks, --answered shows the pair, both nodes and the edge survive, SQL-readable, re-answer replaces, unanswer reopens, pack carries it with a pipe in the note, byte-identical round trip, missing-question record skipped not fatal, merge migration.
